about: What this member said on the floor, from the Congressional Record: their own words only, and of those the sentences that name an alignment question's phrases or make a commitment. Written by npm run record:collect (scripts/collect-record.mjs).
name: Russell Fry

statements.where: Floor speech, Congressional Record: AMERICAN ENRICHMENT DEPLOYMENT ACT
statements.title: AMERICAN ENRICHMENT DEPLOYMENT ACT
sentences: Mr. Speaker, I rise today in support of H.R. 9612, the American Enrichment Deployment Act, legislation I introduced to modernize the outdated licensing process for uranium enrichment facilities and to help restore America's nuclear energy leadership.
By putting these facilities on more equal footing with other parts of the nuclear fuel cycle, we can create a clearer and more predictable pathway for new projects to move forward.
At a time when our country is working to strengthen our nuclear energy capability, we should ensure that outdated regulations do not stand in the way of private sector investment and innovation.
Just as importantly, this effort has brought Republicans and Democrats together around a shared goal of strengthening America's nuclear energy future.

Mr. Speaker, I am proud to have introduced this legislation with my colleagues, and I urge the House to support the American Enrichment Deployment Act so we can remove these unnecessary barriers, strengthen our domestic supply of nuclear energy, and ensure that the United States leads the next generation of that nuclear energy.

statements.where: Floor speech, Congressional Record: SECURE AMERICA ACT
statements.title: SECURE AMERICA ACT
sentences: Mr. Speaker, the Mexican cartels have never had better lobbyists than the Democrat politicians across the aisle who insisted that nothing was wrong for years.
When the border was overwhelmed, they said it was secure.
In fact, they told us that we were imagining a border crisis.
When law enforcement came forward and said we need resources, they were lectured by the ivory tower that Democrats sit in about compassion.
The American people are done being put last at the expense of themselves and put in last place behind illegal immigrants.
Something has been fundamentally wrong with our border for a long time.
We are here on immigration and a border bill, and we are told we are dealing with the economy on their end.
This is about the border and securing the most fundamentally sacred thing in our country, which is our border.
Fund law enforcement and don't defund them.
Mr. Speaker, I urge my colleagues to support this legislation.

statements.where: Floor speech, Congressional Record: SAVING HOMEOWNERS FROM OVERREGULATION WITH EXCEPTIONAL RINSING ACT
statements.title: SAVING HOMEOWNERS FROM OVERREGULATION WITH EXCEPTIONAL RINSING ACT
sentences: You can take showerheads, but the Biden administration also did this on home appliances, gas stoves, any number of things.
We are going to pass this bill, in 1975, and for over 30 years that was the national standard.

Along comes the Obama administration, and rather than take the very simple, easy-to-understand, congressionally mandated standard of what a showerhead is, the Obama administration, in some closet somewhere, decided we are going to reinvent the definition of a showerhead.

statements.where: Floor speech, Congressional Record: KAYLA HAMILTON ACT
statements.title: KAYLA HAMILTON ACT
sentences: In 2022, during the Biden-Harris administration, Kayla's killer illegally crossed the southwest border as an unaccompanied alien child, what they commonly refer to as a ``UAC.'' Walter Javier Martinez, a 16- year-old Salvadoran national, admitted to authorities that his aunt paid a guide $4,000 to smuggle him into the United States.
Despite incomplete information and the sponsor's lack of legal status in the country themselves, HHS approved the placement.

According to his sponsor, months later, Walter left to: ``do what he was doing in his home country--get in trouble on the streets and hang out with gang members.'' The Federal Government just needed to make a phone call to El Salvador.
Instead, Kayla was brutally murdered because the government failed to vet Walter, a known MS-13 gang member with gang tattoos and a criminal history.
Opponents say this provision will lead to the indefinite detention of children.
Next, the bill bars illegal aliens from serving as sponsors.
Walter Javier Martinez was a gang member, and we didn't know it.
Can you imagine going to a State family court and saying to the Judge: Don't worry about the background checks; just send the kid out.
Don't worry about the background checks on the sponsor.
We haven't done the sexual background checks; the sex registry checks.
We haven't done the criminal background checks to see who these sponsors are.

If there is somebody who is smuggled across our border who has a gang affiliation or prior gang convictions or charges in their country of origin, then maybe we shouldn't unite them with their family in this country when they are a danger to themselves and to the rest of society.
I think it was said that the sponsors already receive background checks.

However, in these cases what we saw during the Biden-Harris administration was while the background checks were ongoing and not yet complete, we were sending kids to houses with sponsors without background checks.
The border is secure, but we saw millions of people illegally come into this country causing mayhem.
Kids who are gang members in their country of origin are allowed to go to a sponsor.
Instead of doing background checks on the kids or checking for tattoos, we give them papier-mache projects and ask them to identify their gender if they feel comfortable talking about it.

Rather than take that money that the American people have given to the U.S. Treasury to spend for their safety, we are doing these ridiculous things instead of actually vetting a gang member from El Salvador.
Why are we not conducting adequate background checks on their pasts?
On the flip side of this, I think this is just common sense, that if the law says that sponsors should undergo background checks before we release a kid, sure.
Under the last administration, they were too busy pushing kids to sponsors at a record pace that they never even allowed those background checks of the sponsors to come back.
Mr. Speaker, I rise today in strong support of this legislation, H.R. 4371, the Kayla Hamilton Act.
Mr. Speaker, I will concede very easily that most kids are probably innocent.
That is common sense, but what I have heard is that we are going to keep repeating the same tired lies, the same tired fabrications of what actually is going on in this country.

statements.where: Floor speech, Congressional Record: POWER PLANT RELIABILITY ACT OF 2025
statements.title: POWER PLANT RELIABILITY ACT OF 2025
sentences: Mr. Speaker, I rise in strong support of H.R. 3632, the Power Plant Reliability Act, introduced by my colleague from the Ninth District of Virginia.

statements.where: Floor speech, Congressional Record: TRAFFICKING SURVIVORS RELIEF ACT
statements.title: TRAFFICKING SURVIVORS RELIEF ACT
sentences: We see it happen to a vast number of women and children who are exploited after crossing our southern border.
We see it happen to people from both low-income and high-income backgrounds.

Efforts by Federal, State, and local law enforcement and advocates to eliminate trafficking and to support victims have increased awareness, reporting, and prosecution of sex traffickers across the country.
To ensure that these opportunities are only available to true victims of trafficking and not criminals, we have worked hand in hand with law enforcement to include appropriate safeguards in the bill.

The legislation allows for additional evidence to be considered, including the sworn testimony of a law enforcement officer as to whether a victim had any role in coercing other victims into criminal offenses.
This legislation is endorsed by multiple advocacy organizations, faith-based organizations, and law enforcement officials.
This is a bipartisan, bicameral piece of legislation that unites both law enforcement and victim organizations.
Law enforcement loves this bill, too.
One, it is very therapeutic and helpful to the victims themselves, but for the law enforcement folks, they can go after the real bad actors.
I think that is the key crux of this bill, and I think that is what unites Republicans and Democrats, House and Senate Members, and the law enforcement community and victim organizations.
It is law enforcement-focused, as well.
What they would share with me and what I will share with you today is that this absolutely matters to them.

statements.where: Floor speech, Congressional Record: ONE BIG BEAUTIFUL BILL ACT
statements.title: ONE BIG BEAUTIFUL BILL ACT
sentences: They ignored the border crisis while towns are overrun.
Democrats would rather police our speech than protect our streets.
They will rush to ban plastic straws but look the other way when fentanyl overruns our cities.
It secures the border, and it protects our communities.

statements.where: Floor speech, Congressional Record: FEDERAL LAW ENFORCEMENT OFFICER SERVICE WEAPON PURCHASE ACT OF 2025
statements.title: FEDERAL LAW ENFORCEMENT OFFICER SERVICE WEAPON PURCHASE ACT OF 2025
sentences: Mr. Speaker, pursuant to House Resolution 405, I call up the bill (H.R. 2255) to allow Federal law enforcement officers to purchase retired service weapons, and for other purposes, and ask for its immediate consideration in the House.

Mr. Speaker, H.R. 2255, the Federal Law Enforcement Officer Service Weapon Purchase Act, will allow current or former Federal law enforcement officers in good standing to purchase a retired service weapon at salvage value from the Federal agency that issued the service weapon to the officer.
Current Federal regulations require all Federal law enforcement agencies to destroy their firearms after they are retired from official use.
For example, in 2022, the Fraternal Order of Police notified Congress that multiple Federal law enforcement agencies were in the process of replacing their service weapons.
Law enforcement officers should have the opportunity to purchase the service weapon they used while serving in law enforcement.

This legislation is supported by 10 law enforcement organizations, the Association of State Criminal Investigative Agencies, Federal Law Enforcement Officers Association, the National Fraternal Order of Police, Major Cities Chiefs Association, the Major County Sheriffs of America, the National Association of Police Organizations, the National Narcotics Officers' Associations' Coalition, the National Sheriffs' Association, the Sergeants Benevolent Association NYPD, and the National Treasury Employees Union.
This is a commonsense, cost-saving initiative that supports law enforcement and the American taxpayers.

Mr. Speaker, just to discuss a few of the extraneous comments that were made by the minority party, the officer that is currently employed by a Federal law enforcement agency must be in good standing.
Second of all, grenade launchers are not issued by Federal law enforcement agencies.
They might be used by Federal law enforcement, but they are not issued to that officer.
In the event that the officer is retired within that 6-month period, these weapons don't sit around with their name on them in a locker room somewhere waiting for the weapon to also be retired.
Law enforcement officers put their lives on the line every single day.
Law enforcement officers are not issued machine guns.
This is a commonsense bill supported by a lot of law enforcement agencies, a lot of law enforcement organizations, and was voted on in a bipartisan fashion last Congress.

Mr. Speaker, H.R. 2255, the Federal Law Enforcement Officer Service Weapon Purchase Act, is a very commonsense piece of legislation supported by Republicans and, at least last Congress, by 13 Democrats, as well.
Fourteen Members across the aisle voted in favor of this same exact bill, and I encourage more Members to do so as we honor police this week and into the future.
Law enforcement officers are faced with danger every single day, not only on the job, but when they return to their homes.
The DOGE stuff I won't respond to at all because it doesn't need to be.

statements.where: Floor speech, Congressional Record: IMPROVING LAW ENFORCEMENT OFFICER SAFETY AND WELLNESS THROUGH DATA ACT
statements.title: IMPROVING LAW ENFORCEMENT OFFICER SAFETY AND WELLNESS THROUGH DATA ACT
sentences: Mr. Speaker, pursuant to House Resolution 405, I call up the bill (H.R. 2240) to require the Attorney General to develop reports relating to violent attacks against law enforcement officers, and for other purposes, and ask for its immediate consideration in the House.
Mr. Speaker, police officers risk their lives every day to protect our communities.
I extend my sincere gratitude to all law enforcement officers and their families for their service and sacrifice.
Unfortunately, law enforcement officers face the continued threat of unprovoked and ambush-style attacks.

The bill before us, the Improving Law Enforcement Officer Safety and Wellness Through Data Act, would require the Attorney General to develop a series of reports related to violent attacks on law enforcement officers.

The left's defund the police movement continues to have ripple effects throughout the country, as violent crime remains high and criminals have become more brazen in their attacks against police officers.
Let me be clear: The threat to officer safety is very real, and we must take a stand against any defund the police rhetoric.
This violence against law enforcement is unacceptable and underscores the importance of this legislation.

While the government collects basic information on these attacks, such as when the attack occurred and what types of weapons are used, more information is needed to help law enforcement officers prepare for, identify, and prevent future anti-police activity.
This legislation would also shed light on the mental health consequences of the attacks on law enforcement and other trauma law enforcement deals with on a daily basis.
Mental health resources are another critical need for law enforcement officers, as they continue to risk their lives every day to keep their communities safe.
It will gather more information to help Congress explore the best possible solutions for our law enforcement officers.
Let's all work together to stand against attacks on law enforcement and support our men and women in blue.
Law enforcement has been demonized and attacked.
I hope that that movement is forever in the dustbin of our history because we owe it to law enforcement to support them in any number of ways that we can as policymakers.

Understanding these attacks on our law enforcement, how it is affected by the officer, how these things occur, where they occur, these data points are incredibly important to understand and protect our law enforcement.
I hope that this year even more Democrats will support it and that it will be signed into law because this data is incredibly important to make sure that we protect our law enforcement officers.
I urge all of my colleagues to support it.

statements.where: Floor speech, Congressional Record: HALT ALL LETHAL TRAFFICKING OF FENTANYL ACT
statements.title: HALT ALL LETHAL TRAFFICKING OF FENTANYL ACT
sentences: I rise in strong favor of the HALT Fentanyl Act to combat the deadliest drug crisis our Nation has ever faced.
If this goes away, that is a win for the cartels, criminals, and Chinese Communist Party.
The HALT Fentanyl Act permanently classifies all fentanyl-related substances, analogues, and derivatives as schedule I drugs, ensuring that law enforcement has those necessary tools to do their jobs.
